landing.title:
Turn Sustainability
Into Your Next
Competitive Advantage
landing.subtitle: Sustainability is one of the most underused lenses for innovation. We use it to help organisations spot unmet needs and turn them into breakthrough products, services, and technologies that people want, markets reward, and the future demands.
landing.successstory1: We transformed complex carbon footprint data into a digital tool that made sustainability accessible and actionable for consumers. Presented at COP26 and at the Global Conference for Safety Regulation and Sustainability. Now used by Tesco, Morrisons, and the UK Food Standards Agency.
landing.successstory2: We transformed a simple need—borrowing a drill instead of buying one—into La Trucothèque, a circular service ecosystem co-designed with the ..., local libraries, businesses, students, and citizens. Taking its first steps towards launch across Strasbourg, the project shows how our Sustainable Innovation Method creates shared value through synergy-oriented innovation.
landing.successstory3: We are transforming local renewable energy into a shared community asset. Power to the People enables neighbours to share locally generated solar electricity, creating lower energy costs, greater energy independence, and stronger, more resilient communities. Currently in the start-up phase.

hero.title:
Sustainability isn't the problem.
The real challenge is turning it into innovation.
hero.subtitle:
Businesses know sustainability matters. What they struggle with is turning it into value.
  • What are the real opportunities?
  • How do we stay ahead of regulation?
  • How do we create solutions people choose?
  • How do we align the right partners to make it happen?
That's where we come in.

whatIdo.title: Our philosophy — your competitive advantage
whatIdo.subtitle: People, Planet, & Prosperity
whatIdo.text1: Products, services and business models that respond to real human needs, improve experiences and create social value.
whatIdo.text2: Solutions that respect ecological limits, reduce environmental harm and contribute to healthier, more resilient ecosystems.
whatIdo.text3: New opportunities for businesses to innovate, differentiate, build stronger relationships and create lasting economic value.
whatIdo.intro: Business success does not happen in isolation. Businesses depend on people, communities, natural resources and healthy ecosystems. Ignoring these dependencies can create risks; understanding them can reveal opportunities for innovation, resilience and long-term value.
whatIdo.lead: My approach brings three dimensions together:
whatIdo.closing1: These dimensions are interconnected, not interchangeable. A commercially successful solution that creates environmental harm is not sustainable; nor is an environmentally sound idea that fails to meet people's needs or work in practice.
whatIdo.closing2: The ambition is to find opportunities where these dimensions reinforce one another — creating value for business, society and the living world.

gozel.title: Dr Gözel Shakeri
gozel.text:
I help organisations turn sustainability from a compliance challenge into a source of innovation and competitive advantage. Through my Sustainable Innovation Method, I combine human-centred design, sustainable digitalisation, and systems thinking to identify the products, services, technologies, and business models that people genuinely want—and the future demands.

My work has helped organisations tackle complex sustainability challenges, from transforming digital customer experiences to redesigning services and developing more sustainable ways of living and working. I have partnered with industry leaders, including Tesco, government organisations such as the Food Standards Agency, and NGOs including WWF-UK to translate research into practical, commercially relevant innovation.

I hold a PhD in Human–Computer Interaction (HCI) from the University of Glasgow, where my thesis was shortlisted for the Best Computing Science PhD in Scotland. My research into sustainable innovation and digital behaviour has also been recognised with an Outstanding Young Scientists Award for reimagining sustainable consumer experiences.

Beyond consulting, I regularly advise, teach, and speak on sustainable innovation. I have contributed to international initiatives including COP26, the UN Game Changers Lab, and the Global Conference for Safety Regulation and Sustainability, helping organisations understand how good innovation can unlock successful sustainability transitions.

Today, I work with businesses, governments, and research organisations to discover future opportunities, align stakeholders, and design innovations that create lasting value for people, business, and the planet.
gozel.teamtext: I have an extensive international network of experts I call on for engagements. My collaborators come from backgrounds in behaviour change, digital tech law, and design research.
gozel.subtitle1text: Start with humans, not policies, tools, or technologies.
gozel.subtitle2text: I believe that people do better work and are more creative when they are having fun.
gozel.subtitle3text: Teams are better when they work together, harnessing the diversity and complexity of the group.
gozel.subtitle4text: I foster a “yes, and” environment in which people accept and build on each others’ ideas.

hcd.title: Human-centered Design
hcd.abstract: My work is grounded in human-centered design — a creative problem-solving framework for leading and engaging with empathy and designing innovative solutions to complex problems.
hcd.whatanswers:
Human-centered design (ISO standard ISO 9241-210:2019), also referred to as design thinking, is a problem-solving process, by being predominantly solution-focused. It is comprised of robust methods and core mindsets that, when practiced together, allow people to collaborate, communicate, and work differently.

It involves discovering and understanding customer needs, defining and identifying opportunities, exploring and developing options, and delivering solutions by building and testing prototypes.
hcd.approach1answers: Using design thinking, I can help you transform your approach to problem-solving and innovation. This human-centered framework empowers businesses to craft impactful solutions while enabling professionals to become more adaptable, creative, and effective in their roles.
hcd.approach2answers: By combining qualitative and quantitative insights with rapid prototyping and testing, I uncover the full story — revealing deeper needs, motivations, and behaviors to drive smarter, more impactful decisions for your success.
hcd.approach3answers: By integrating evidence-based behavioral science frameworks such as the Behavior Change Wheel and Motive Disposition Theory, I craft strategies and solutions that inspire lasting change, deepen engagement, and strengthen resilience.
hcd.divider2: HCD is embedded in my approach to ...

approach.title: The Sustainable Innovation Method
approach.subtitle: turns complex sustainability challenges into practical solutions that create value for business, society, and policymakers.
approach.problemtitle: Three pillars of the Sustainable Innovation Method
approach.problemanswer: We believe lasting innovation requires a positive mindset. However, most respond to sustainability with caution, compliance, and constraint. We do something different: we dream, design, and build.
approach.whatanswers: Sustainability conversations are often constrained by
approach.whatanswers1:
Siloed teams, competing stakeholder priorities, and legacy ways of working create fragmented decision-making and prevent effective action.

Synergise: How can everyone contribute and benefit?
approach.whatanswers2:
Anxiety, sacrifice, guilt, and hopelessness make it harder for people to imagine—and create—better ways forward.

Imagine: What breakthrough technologies can we create?
approach.whatanswers3:
Ever-shifting laws, complex climate reporting, and hollow sustainability exercises, breed both exhaustion and a deepening cynicism about whether efforts truly matter.

Reframe: What opportunities does sustainability create?
approach.whatanswers4: When these barriers reinforce one another, sustainability becomes a crisis organisations manage and respond to—rather than an opportunity to innovate.
approach.whatanswers5title: Change the way you see sustainability: change what's possible.
approach.whatanswers5:
Grounded in over a decade of academic research and industry collaboration, we developed the Sustainable Innovation Method. Its three pillars are designed to overcome these barriers, open up new possibilities, and turn ambitious ideas into action.

Lead the future, don’t just adapt to it.
approach.step2text: Design futures people want to build.
approach.step3text: Design for people, systems, and generations.
approach.step4text: Build the innovations that define what's next.
approach.approach1answers:
Understand what prevents people from engaging—and what motivates them instead.

The challenge:
For many people, sustainability feels like sacrifice: consuming less, giving up more, and accepting new constraints for benefits that often seem distant or beyond their control. Even as climate change becomes more tangible, feelings of powerlessness (in the face of global weather events) make it harder for organisations to inspire change, drive adoption, and innovate.

Our approach:
Our Sustainable Innovation Method helps organisations move beyond these barriers. Combining behavioural science, human-centred design, and proprietary innovation tools, we uncover what people genuinely need, value, and aspire to - even in and despite climate change.

Your organisation gains:
Evidence-based insight into stakeholder needs, motivations, and behaviours. A clear understanding of the organisational and behavioural barriers limiting innovation. A shift from viewing sustainability as a compliance challenge to seeing it as a strategic opportunity.
approach.approach2answers:
Lead the future instead of reacting to it.

The challenge:
Lasting change requires more than a strategy—it requires a compelling vision of the future. We help organisations define a future that employees want to work towards, customers want to be part of, and stakeholders want to invest in. Because organisations that shape the future don't wait for change—they lead it.

Our approach:
Our Sustainable Innovation Method helps imagining futures that people genuinely want to be part of. Using insights from behavioural science and tools from futures thinking and design thinking, we create ambitious yet credible solutions that strengthen hope, agency, and shared purpose—providing a clear direction for innovation.

Your organisation gains:
Aligned customers, employees, and stakeholders around a shared future. Greater confidence and ambition to innovate beyond incremental improvements. A strategic foundation for developing products, services, and economically sustainable business models that people are excited to adopt.
approach.approach3answers:
No transition happens in isolation — we design for the whole system.

The challenge:
Many sustainable innovations fail because they optimise for one stakeholder while overlooking the wider system. Conflicting priorities, unintended consequences, and misaligned incentives create resistance, slow implementation, and limit long-term impact.

Our approach:
Our Sustainable Innovation Method expands design beyond the end user. Using systems thinking, stakeholder mapping, and collaborative co-design, we identify where interests align, uncover opportunities for shared value, and design innovations that work across the entire ecosystem.

Your organisation gains:
A shared understanding of the wider system and the stakeholders shaping success. Stronger alignment across partners and decision-makers. Solutions that are more resilient, easier to implement, and more widely adopted because they create value for everyone involved.
approach.approach4answers: With people, futures, and systems understood, we generate real solutions — new products, services, technologies, and business models — using tools like the Sustainable Innovation Canvas (download here).
approach.reason1answer: Grounded in behavioural science, Human–Computer Interaction, systems thinking, and sustainability research—not assumptions.
approach.reason2answer: Designed around how people actually think, decide, and adopt innovation.
approach.reason3answer: Recognises that meaningful innovation emerges across organisations, sectors, and communities—not in isolation.
approach.reason4answer: Moves sustainability beyond compliance to identify new markets, products, and business models.
approach.reason5answer:
You will be better equipped to:
  • Spot emerging market opportunities early
  • Build innovations customers genuinely value
  • Reduce uncertainty before investing
  • Align stakeholders around one shared future
  • Strengthen adoption of what you launch
  • Create business models built to last
approach.reason6answer:
The organisations that lead the sustainability transition won't just adapt to change.

They'll create the products, services, and experiences that define it.

privacypolicy.title: Privacy Policy
privacypolicy.content:
This privacy policy will explain how Shakeri et al. uses the personal data we collect from you when you use our website.

Topics:

  • What data do we collect?
  • What are your data protection rights?
  • Changes to our privacy policy
  • How to contact us

What data do we collect?

Shakeri et al. collects the following data:

  • None

What are your data protection rights?

Shakeri et al. would like to make sure you are fully aware of all of your data protection rights. Every user is entitled to the following:

  • The right to access - You have the right to request Shakeri et al. for copies of your personal data. We may charge you a small fee for this service.
  • The right to rectification - You have the right to request that Shakeri et al. correct any information you believe is inaccurate. You also have the right to request Shakeri et al. to complete information you believe is incomplete.
  • The right to erasure - You have the right to request that Shakeri et al. erase your personal data, under certain conditions.
  • The right to restrict processing - You have the right to request that Shakeri et al. restrict the processing of your personal data, under certain conditions.
  • The right to object to processing - You have the right to object to Shakeri et al.'s processing of your personal data, under certain conditions.
  • The right to data portability - You have the right to request that Shakeri et al. transfer the data that we have collected to another organization, or directly to you, under certain conditions.

Check out the EU's GDPR regulation here: https://gdpr-info.eu/

Changes to our privacy policy

Shakeri et al. keeps its privacy policy under regular review and places any updates on this web page. This privacy policy was last updated on 20/03/2025.

How to contact us

If you have any questions about Shakeri et al.'s privacy policy, please do not hesitate to contact us.

Email us at: gozel@shakeri.eu

researchpage.faq4q: Do you work on-site or remotely?
researchpage.faq4a: Both: in person in the Strasbourg–Eurométropole region, and remotely everywhere else.

researchpage.faq5a: Yes. We can run studies together with your team and train them in the methods along the way.
